13427-notes-and-queries-number-45-septem.title: Notes And Queries Number 45 September 7 1850
13427-notes-and-queries-number-45-septem.creator: Unknown
13427-notes-and-queries-number-45-septem.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. _The First Mole in Cornwall; a Morality from the Stowe of Morwenna, in the Rocky Land._--A lonely life for the dark and silent mole! She glides along her narrow vaults, unconscious of the glad and glorious scenes of earth, and air, and sea! She was born, as it were, in a grave, and in one long living sepulchre she dwells and dies!

arxiv-2105-15014.title: SINGING LANGUAGE IDENTIFICATION USING A DEEP PHONOTACTIC APPROACH
arxiv-2105-15014.creator: Lenny Renault, Andrea Vaglio, Romain Hennequin
arxiv-2105-15014.description: Abstract Extensive works have tackled LID ( LID ) in the speech domain, however their application to the singing voice trails and performances on SLID ( SLID ) can be improved leveraging recent progresses made in other singing related tasks.

arxiv-2106-07054.title: Inferring the mixing properties of an ergodic process
arxiv-2106-07054.creator: Azadeh Khaleghi, Gábor Lugosi
arxiv-2106-07054.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Azadeh Khaleghi, Gábor Lugosi. We propose strongly consistent estimators of the ℓ 1 \ell_{1} norm of the sequence of α \alpha -mixing (respectively β \beta -mixing) coefficients of a stationary ergodic process. We further provide strongly consistent estimators of individual α \alpha -mixing (respectively β \beta -mixing) coefficients for a subclass of stationary α \alpha -mixing (respectively β \beta -mixing) processes with summable sequences of mixing coefficients. The estimators are in turn used to develop strongly consistent goodness-of-fit hypothesis tests.

arxiv-2310-05172.title: Systematic Evaluation of Randomized Cache Designs against Cache Occupancy
arxiv-2310-05172.creator: Anirban ChakrabortyMax Planck Institute for Security and Privacy anirban.chakraborty@mpi-sp.org, Nimish MishraIndian Institute of Technology Kharagpur nimish.mishra@kgpian.iitkgp.ac.in Sayandeep SahaIndian Institute of Technology Bombay sayandeepsaha@cse.iitb.ac.in Sarani BhattacharyaIndian Institut
arxiv-2310-05172.description: Abstract Randomizing the address-to-set mapping and partitioning of the cache has been shown to be an effective mechanism in designing secured caches. Several designs have been proposed on a variety of rationales: ① randomized design, ② randomized-and-partitioned design, and ③ psuedo-fully associative design.

arxiv-2402-15917.title: A Finite Element Model for Hydro-thermal Convective Flow in a Porous Medium: Effects of Hydraulic Resistivity and Thermal Diffusivity
arxiv-2402-15917.creator: S. M. Mallikarjunaiah, Dambaru Bhatta
arxiv-2402-15917.description: Abstract In this article, a finite element model is implemented to analyze hydro-thermal convective flow in a porous medium. The mathematical model encompasses Darcy’s law for incompressible fluid behavior, which is coupled with a convection-diffusion-type energy equation to characterize the temperature in the porous medium.

arxiv-2409-01366.title: CHESS : Optimizing LLM Inference via Channel-Wise Thresholding and Selective Sparsification
arxiv-2409-01366.creator: Junhui He, Shangyu Wu, Weidong Wen, Chun Jason Xue, Qingan Li
arxiv-2409-01366.description: Abstract Deploying large language models (LLMs) on edge devices presents significant challenges due to the substantial computational overhead and memory requirements. Activation sparsification can mitigate these resource challenges by reducing the number of activated neurons during inference. Existing methods typically employ thresholding-based sparsification based on the statistics of activation tensors.

arxiv-2410-12012.title: Evolution of the universe with quintessence model in Rastall gravity
arxiv-2410-12012.creator: J. K. Singh, Akanksha Singh, Shaily, Sushant G. Ghosh, Sunil D. Maharaj
arxiv-2410-12012.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by J. K. Singh, Akanksha Singh, Shaily, Sushant G. Ghosh, Sunil D. Maharaj. We investigate the universe’s evolution within the framework of Rastall gravity, which is an extension of the standard Λ \Lambda CDM model.

arxiv-2503-14684.creator: Mojtaba Esfandiari, Pengyuan Du, Haochen Wei, Graduate Student Member, IEEE, Peter Gehlbach, Adnan Munawar, Peter Kazanzides, Member, IEEE, Iulian Iordachita, Senior Member, IEEE

arxiv-2507-14349.title: Analysis note: measurement of thrust in 𝒆 + ​ 𝒆 − e^{+}e^{-} collisions at 𝒔 \sqrt{s} = 91 GeV with archived ALEPH data
arxiv-2507-14349.creator: Anthony Badea, Austin Baty, Hannah Bossi, Yu-Chen Chen, Yi Chen, Jingyu Zhang, Gian Michele Innocenti, Marcello Maggi, Chris McGinn, Michael Peters, Tzu-An Sheng, Vinicius Mikuni, Matthew Avaylon, Patrick Komiske, Eric Metodiev, Jesse Thaler, Benjamin Nachman, Yen-Jie Lee
arxiv-2507-14349.description: Abstract A measurement of the thrust distribution in e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} collisions at s = 91.2 \sqrt{s}=91.2 GeV with archived data from the ALEPH experiment at the Large Electron-Positron Collider is presented. The thrust distribution is reconstructed from charged and neutral particles resulting from hadronic Z Z -boson decays.

arxiv-2509-16617.title: Detection and Simulation of Urban Heat Islands Using a Fine-Tuned Geospatial Foundation Model
arxiv-2509-16617.creator: David Kreismann
arxiv-2509-16617.description: Abstract As urbanization and climate change progress, urban heat island effects are becoming more frequent and severe. To formulate effective mitigation plans, cities require detailed air temperature data. However, predictive analytics methods based on conventional machine learning models and limited data infrastructure often provide inaccurate predictions, especially in underserved areas.

pmc-10724433.title: Recent Advances in Sensor–Actuator Hybrid Soft Systems: Core Advantages, Intelligent Applications, and Future Perspectives (Adv. Sci. 35/2023)
pmc-10724433.creator: Chankyu Han, Yongrok Jeong, Junseong Ahn, Taehwan Kim, Jungrak Choi, Ji‐Hwan Ha, Hyunjin Kim, Soon Hyoung Hwang, Sohee Jeon, Jihyeon Ahn, Jin Tae Hong, Jin Joo Kim, Jun‐Ho Jeong, Inkyu Park
pmc-10724433.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Sensor–Actuator Hybrid Soft Systems In article number 2302775, Jun‐Ho Jeong, Inkyu Park, and co‐workers present an in‐depth review article that offers an encompassing examination of contemporary progress within sensor and actuator integrated systems. The discussed advancements are systematically classified into three distinct categories, characterized by their primary functionalities: (i) actuator–assisted sensors for intelligent detection, (ii) sensor‐assisted actuators for intelligent movement, and (iii) sensor‐actuator interactive devices for a hybrid of intelligent detection and movement.

pmc-10765038.title: Microbial Primer: In vivo biofilm
pmc-10765038.creator: Kendra P. Rumbaugh, Thomas Bjarnsholt
pmc-10765038.description: In this primer on biofilms and their role in infections, we trace the historical roots of microbial understanding from Van Leeuwenhoek’s observations to Bill Costerton’s groundbreaking work, which solidified biofilms' significance in infections. In vivo biofilm research, investigating patient samples and utilizing diverse host models, has yielded invaluable insights into these complex microbial communities.

pmc-11503381.title: Pathophysiology and Prevention of Manual-Ventilation-Induced Lung Injury (MVILI)
pmc-11503381.creator: Luke A. White, Steven A. Conrad, Jonathan Steven Alexander
pmc-11503381.description: Manual ventilation, most commonly with a bag-valve mask, is a form of short-term ventilation used during resuscitative efforts in emergent and out-of-hospital scenarios. However, compared to mechanical ventilation, manual ventilation is an operator-dependent skill that is less well controlled and is highly subject to providing inappropriate ventilation to the patient.

pmc-11566348.title: Association of cartilage T1ρ and T2 relaxation time measurement with hip osteoarthritis progression: A 5-year longitudinal study using voxel-based relaxometry and Z-score normalization
pmc-11566348.creator: Rafeek Thahakoya, Koren E. Roach, Misung Han, Rupsa Bhattacharjee, Fei Jiang, Johanna Luitjens, Emma Bahroos, Valentina Pedoia, Richard B. Souza, Sharmila Majumdar
pmc-11566348.description: ObjectiveTo study the longitudinal changes of cartilage T1ρ and T2 relaxation time measurements in hip-OA patients.MethodsA calibration study compared two scanner data, Scanner-1 (GE Discovery MR750 3.0T) with unilateral acquisition protocol and Scanner-2 (GE Signa Premier 3.0T) with bilateral acquisition protocol, using nine subjects(average age ​= ​40.33 ​± ​13.53 years, 5 females), including one hip-OA subject.

pmc-11690872.title: GOING BOLDER: PROMOTING DEMENTIA INFRASTRUCTURE THROUGH INTERACTIVE AND AI WEB-BASED TOOLS
pmc-11690872.creator: Nicole Ruggiano, Monica Herzog, Zhe Jiang, Ellen Brown, Vagelis Hristidis, Jane Daquin
pmc-11690872.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Congress successfully passed the Building Our Largest Dementia (BOLD) Infrastructure for Alzheimer’s Act to advance public health initiatives that support people living with dementia (PLWD) and their families. Part of the goals of BOLD include advancing community awareness about the latest research on dementia and support the translation of research findings to support PLWD, their families, and providers in addressing needs related to dementia care and caregiving.

pmc-13378008.title: ZDHHC17-mediated IKKβ palmitoylation suppresses NF-κB signaling to mitigate the progression of liver fibrosis
pmc-13378008.creator: Bin Fan, Meng Yi, Xiaolong Zhong, Shilin Li, Chunhui Yang, Peng Zhang, Daping Song, Qing Xiao, Yujia Li, Xiaoqiong Duan, Limin Chen
pmc-13378008.description: SummaryLiver fibrosis (LF) is a common consequence of chronic liver injury and inflammation, driven by the IKK complex-mediated NF-κB signaling pathway. This study investigated the role of macrophage IKKβ palmitoylation in NF-κB signaling and LF progression. Analysis of liver tissues and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from LF patients and healthy individuals revealed decreased ZDHHC17 expression in LF-associated macrophages.

pmc-13416896.title: An Analysis of the Sources of Ultrafine Particles During Severe Haze Pollution Periods in China
pmc-13416896.creator: Jingkun Zhou, Long Sun, Yunkai Zhou
pmc-13416896.description: Haze Pollution in China arises from the rapid enlargement of ultrafine particles into light-absorbing fine particulate matter through adsorption processes under atmospheric stagnation conditions. This study focuses on the sources of ultrafine particles (UFPs), the most critical component of haze pollutants during severe pollution periods in China.

pmc-13500661.title: Proton trap engineered electric swing adsorption for scalable and cost-effective direct air capture
pmc-13500661.creator: Yao Shen, Kai Pang, Weichen Zhao, Liang Chen, Jingkai Zhao, Jiexu Ye, Beini Zhang, Sujing Li, Wei Li, Zhen Xu, Jing Meng, Xiang Gao, Shihan Zhang
pmc-13500661.description: Direct air capture (DAC) is critical to achieve carbon neutrality, yet current technologies face significant barriers to widespread, cost-effective deployment. Amine-based electric swing adsorption (ESA) offers a promising low-energy, steam-free pathway, but its efficiency is fundamentally limited by an inherent 2:1 amine-to-CO2 stoichiometric penalty.

pmc-13584320.title: Vulvar Apocrine Hidrocystoma: A Rare Case Report
pmc-13584320.creator: Nastaran Mahmoudnejad, Peyman Mohammadi Torbati, Niloofar Irandoost
pmc-13584320.description: Apocrine hidrocystoma is a rare and benign tumor that usually occurs on the head, neck, and face. Involvement of the vulva is extremely rare, with only a few documented case reports in the literature. The prognosis of the tumor is favorable with surgical excision, with no reported recurrences.
